notes.headline: This mix is in good shape for mastering — the only real issue is that the file stops while audio is still playing at full level.
notes.summary: At -14.38 LUFS integrated with -1.27 dBTP true peak and 13.1 dB peak-to-loudness, you've left plenty of headroom and dynamics for a mastering engineer to work with. Stereo behaviour is solid too: 0.785 L/R correlation, 0.793 in the low end, only 0.5 dB mono loss, and the channels are balanced within 0.02 dB. The one thing to fix is the ending — the audio is still loud at the last sample, so the file is likely cut off mid-tail. Re-export with the tails included and this is done.

priorities.title: Ending is cut off
priorities.why: The bounce ends at full level, which means reverb and delay tails are being chopped. A mastering engineer can't restore what isn't in the file, and an abrupt cut reads as a click or a truncated song on playback.

listen_for: Play the last few seconds of the re-exported file and confirm the reverb and delay tails decay fully instead of stopping dead.
Check the very end on headphones at raised volume — any remaining click or sudden silence means the selection still needs extending.
strengths: -1.27 dBTP true peak and -14.38 LUFS leave the headroom a mastering engineer needs.
13.1 dB peak-to-loudness with 6.05 LU loudness range — the dynamics haven't been squashed.
Stereo image is trustworthy: 0.793 low-end correlation, 0.5 dB mono loss, 0.02 dB left/right balance.
